I mean if they don't care, I don't care so tysm is voting incorrectly for sure, I can't tell whether prysm votes correctly because they all abstained their vote, likely offline might not be worth debugging, need actual prysm nodes online, if toni keeps sending those payloads that are late and have 0 blobs it's easy to see tysm is essentially one commit behind prysm's glammy7 head. The commit is for reorging late blocks on slot 31. Other than that, seems like there's no real diff for the PTC codebase. The changes: swap PTC validation verdict + surpress/delay/mutate wire copy + a prometheus copy. last time the ptc hook was turned on was 2D ago. Atleast according to claude this indicates the bug is likely in prysm upstream and not in tysm. how do we wanna move ahead? i can swap out my tysm nodes for prysm so that we have a clean setup for now? then we re-trigger the test and see if it happens again? > how do we wanna move ahead? can your claude fix the prysm code or do we need to ping potuz? 😁 potuz isn't sure that there is a prysm bug or he's only being paid to come up with new ways to be a pain in the ass (e.g epbs) and not to fix bugs 😂 but this one should be easy, if there are 0 blobs, then ptc votes cannot vote unavailable, it's impossible condition claude is on it 😄 backporting a fix they had on develop: https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17316 should fix it but yeah its a prysm bug they already fixed in develop and not a tysm bug ah yeah https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17316/changes/dcee2368a7385362113ed4a2e3233a948e679b99 looks like it fixes it yeah the pr just backports it ok so only lighthouse that is remaining why if the payload was not released? with "late" payload I'm talking about a few min later it was released I started releasing at ~11.4s and increased the delay over time I didn't check the timings but https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-7.ethpandaops.io/slot/165502 says orphaned, pretty sure availability should be separate from payload reveal/timeliness that's why we have 2 separate votes in the ptc message, but potuz can clarify that probably, at least that's what I would expect how it should work from fork choice pov, the availability vote is kinda irrelevant right now if payload is untimely that slot had blobs really https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-7.ethpandaops.io/slot/165502, is dora lying then? oh im looking at the wrong slot ah this bug was fixed like a week or two ago we just havent merged it into devnet-7 my b, ill update devnet-7 branch now I have the same problem, I stopped porting stuff to devnet-7 branch no need to fix this, I just wanted to point it out in case it was not yet noticed What I was doing was bursting the network with batches of late payloads to cause the ELs to do additional validation work it isn't really ready to. Basically, the problem I see is that when publishing a late payload, EL clients will receive it from their CL and validate it. If this means the payload of the current block gets delayed (which is the case afaict), then you eat into execution time of the next slot. I did 3 such bursts and as you can see, I kept my reth node quite busy during a slot in which it should execute another block: This might be fine as the attack costs buying bids (bids don't need to be consecutive slots which helps as otherwise mev would go up). So with 0.1 eth you could "buy" a burst of 10 payloads. My reth node was busy for 6s executing that. Not sure there is a clean solution to this, any one could probably something similar today, just with the full block, but because of using the full slot for execution (or min. 6s to be precise), this might be a bigger problem than today(?) Thinking about it more, the solution might just be demoting builders when not releasing a payload. Every non released payload could cause work in another slot as long as the slot in which the payload was withhold isn't finalized. So maybe clients should block builders until the slot finalizes (or for 3 epochs to keep things simpler). Then builders cannot collect many withhold payloads that could be released to dos another validator. Slot 167589 is an example.
